evolution_chain.description: Original ERISA enactment — four-duty structure established; exclusive benefit, prudent man standard (common law trust), diversification, plan document compliance
Regulatory clarification — DOL issued Interpretive Bulletin 96-1 (1996); fiduciary status analysis for advice-giving; investment policy statement guidance
Pension Protection Act 2006 — added investment advice fiduciary provisions; automatic enrollment safe harbors; default investment alternatives
Current text — post-PPA 2006; DOL cybersecurity guidance 2021 defines prudent expert baseline for identity verification and unauthorized account changes

case_law.key_holding: ERISA benefit decisions by a plan administrator operating under a conflict of interest are reviewed de novo unless the plan grants the administrator discretionary authority
Employer who acts in dual capacity as plan administrator is an ERISA fiduciary when making representations about benefits; individual § 1132(a)(3) relief available

cases_to_add: Tibble v. Edison International (2015) — fiduciary's ongoing duty of prudent monitoring; breach clock runs from each failure to review

citizen_relevance: Case #37 — UA Local 342 Pension Identity Replacement. The Trust administrator who processed an unauthorized retirement election for a 44-year-old journeyman plumber without verifying identity or investigating red flags violated all four §1104(a) duties. Exclusive benefit violated (served identity replacement scheme). Prudent expert violated (no verification of a 44-year-old claiming retirement). Plan document violated (retirement application not signed by participant). §1105 co-fiduciary liability if any trustee knew of the scheme. §1109 damages not capped at accrued benefits.
